additionalProperties.description: Object type for adaptive request properties. This includes most of the environment variables that are supplied by the associated server.

_AdaptiveRequestProperties_.description: Object type for adaptive request properties. This includes most of the environment variables that are supplied by the associated server.

ACCEPT.description: A list of the media types the client can accept.
ACCEPT.title: A list of the media types the client can accept

AUTH_TYPE.description: The authentication method used to validate a user. This is blank if the request did not require authentication.
AUTH_TYPE.title: The authentication method used to validate a user

CONTENT_LENGTH.description: The length of the data (in bytes) passed to the CGI program via standard input.
CONTENT_LENGTH.title: The length of the data (in bytes) passed to the CGI program via standard input

CONTENT_TYPE.description: The media type of the request body, such as 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'.
CONTENT_TYPE.title: The media type of the request body

DOCUMENT_ROOT.description: The directory from which static documents are served.
DOCUMENT_ROOT.title: The directory from which static documents are served

FCGI_ROLE.description: The role component sets the role the Web server expects the application to play. The currently-defined roles are:  RESPONDER, AUTHORIZER, FILTER.
FCGI_ROLE.title: Sets the role the Web server expects the application to play

GATEWAY_INTERFACE.description: The revision of the Common Gateway Interface that the server uses.
GATEWAY_INTERFACE.title: The revision of the Common Gateway Interface that the server uses

HTTPS.description: This variable can be used as a flag to indicate whether the connection is secure; its values vary by server (e.g., 'ON' or 'on' when secure and blank or 'OFF' when not).
HTTPS.title: This variable can be used as a flag to indicate whether the connection is secure

HTTP_ACCEPT.description: A list of the media types the client can accept.
HTTP_ACCEPT.title: A list of the media types the client can accept

HTTP_ACCEPT_CHARSET.description: A list of the character sets the client can accept.
HTTP_ACCEPT_CHARSET.title: A list of the character sets the client can accept

HTTP_ACCEPT_ENCODING.description: A list of the encodings the client can accept.
HTTP_ACCEPT_ENCODING.title: A list of the encodings the client can accept

HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE.description: A list of the languages the client can accept.
HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE.title: A list of the languages the client can accept

HTTP_COOKIE.description: A name-value pair previously set by the server.
HTTP_COOKIE.title: A name-value pair previously set by the server

HTTP_FROM.description: The email address of the user making the request; most browsers do not pass this information, since it is considered an invasion of the user's privacy.
HTTP_FROM.title: The email address of the user making the request

HTTP_HOST.description: The hostname of the server from the requested URL (this corresponds to the HTTP 1.1 Host field).
HTTP_HOST.title: The hostname of the server from the requested URL

HTTP_REFERER.description: The URL of the document that directed the user to this CGI program (e.g., via a hyperlink or via a form).
HTTP_REFERER.title: The URL of the document that directed the user to this CGI program

HTTP_USER_AGENT.description: The name and version of the client's browser.
HTTP_USER_AGENT.title: The name and version of the client's browser

PATH_INFO.description: Extra path information passed to a CGI program.
PATH_INFO.title: Extra path information passed to a CGI program

PATH_TRANSLATED.description: The translated version of the path given by the variable PATH_INFO.
PATH_TRANSLATED.title: The translated version of the path given by the variable PATH_INFO

QUERY_STRING.description: The query information from requested URL (i.e., the data following '?').
QUERY_STRING.title: The query information from requested URL

REMOTE_ADDR.description: The remote IP address of the client making the request; this could be the address of an HTTP proxy between the server and the user.
REMOTE_ADDR.title: The remote IP address of the client making the request

REMOTE_HOST.description: The remote hostname of the client making the request; this could also be the name of an HTTP proxy between the server and the user.
REMOTE_HOST.title: The remote hostname of the client making the request

REMOTE_IDENT.description: The user making the request, as reported by their ident daemon. Only some Unix and IRC users are likely to have this running.
REMOTE_IDENT.title: The user making the request, as reported by their ident daemon

REMOTE_PORT.description: The port number used by the client.
REMOTE_PORT.title: The port number used by the client

REMOTE_USER.description: The user's login, authenticated by the web server.
REMOTE_USER.title: The user's login, authenticated by the web server

REQUEST_METHOD.description: The HTTP request method used for this request.
REQUEST_METHOD.title: The HTTP request method used for this request

REQUEST_SCHEME.description: The scheme of the request (usually 'http' or 'https').
REQUEST_SCHEME.title: The scheme of the request

REQUEST_URI.description: The URI for this request relative to DOCUMENT_ROOT.
REQUEST_URI.title: The URI for this request relative to DOCUMENT_ROOT

SCHEME.description: The scheme of the request (usually 'http' or 'https').
SCHEME.title: The scheme of the request

SCRIPT_NAME.description: The URL path (e.g., /cgi/program.cgi) of the script being executed.
SCRIPT_NAME.title: The URL path (e.g., /cgi/program.cgi) of the script being executed

SERVER_ADDR.description: The IP address of the computer running the web server.
SERVER_ADDR.title: The IP address of the computer running the web server

SERVER_ADMIN.description: The email address for your server's webmaster.
SERVER_ADMIN.title: The email address for your server's webmaster

SERVER_NAME.description: The server's hostname or IP address.
SERVER_NAME.title: The server's hostname or IP address

SERVER_PORT.description: The port number of the host on which the server is listening.
SERVER_PORT.title: The port number of the host on which the server is listening

SERVER_PROTOCOL.description: The name and revision of the request protocol, e.g., 'HTTP/1.1'.
SERVER_PROTOCOL.title: The name and revision of the request protocol

SERVER_SIGNATURE.description:
The HTML string that may be embedded in the page to identify this host.
For example, <ADDRESS>/Apache/1.3.14 Server at www.zytrax.com Port 80</ADDRESS>
SERVER_SIGNATURE.title: The HTML string that may be embedded in the page to identify this host

SERVER_SOFTWARE.description: The name and version of the server software that is answering the client request.
SERVER_SOFTWARE.title: The name and version of the server software that is answering the client request

SSL_CLIENT_M_SERIAL.description: The SSL client certificate serial number.
SSL_CLIENT_M_SERIAL.title: SSL client certificate serial number

SSL_CLIENT_S_DN.description: The SSL client certificate subject DN field.
SSL_CLIENT_S_DN.title: SSL client certificate subject DN

SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_CN.description: The SSL client certificate subject component of the DN field.
SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_CN.title: SSL client certificate subject CN

SSL_CLIENT_VERIFY.description: The SSL client certificate verification result. May be NONE, SUCCESS, GENEROUS or FAILED:reason.
SSL_CLIENT_VERIFY.title: SSL client certificate verification result

SSL_CLIENT_V_REMAIN.description: Number of days until client's certificate expires.
SSL_CLIENT_V_REMAIN.title: Number of days until client's certificate expires
